title: Sticky
summary: Headers that stay at the top while their section scrolls are LazyColumn's stickyHeader, and bars fixed to an edge are the topBar and bottomBar of a Scaffold. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: stickyHeader for group headers of a long list (letters of a contact list, days of an activity feed). Scaffold's topBar and bottomBar for a filter bar or an action bar that is always at the top or bottom; pass the Scaffold's content padding to the list so nothing is hidden behind them.
whenNotToUse: Do not pin more than one header at a time, and do not pin content in a short screen that does not scroll. For a top app bar that collapses on scroll use TopAppBar with a TopAppBarScrollBehavior.
api: fun LazyListScope.stickyHeader(key: Any? = null, contentType: Any? = null, content: @Composable LazyItemScope.(Int) -> Unit)

@Composable fun Scaffold(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, topBar: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, bottomBar: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, snackbarHost: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, floatingActionButton: @Composable () -> Unit = {}, ..., content: @Composable (PaddingValues) -> Unit)

states.name: stuck
states.description: Read from the list state: derivedStateOf { state.firstVisibleItemIndex > 0 || state.firstVisibleItemScrollOffset > 0 } is true once content scrolls under the header; use it to add a divider or a shadow.

appearance: A sticky header needs an opaque background (the surface color) so rows do not show through it. A bar in a Scaffold uses the Material 3 colors mapped from the Monarch theme.
platformNotes: The web Sticky pins any element to the top or bottom with an offset, adds a shadow when stuck (elevateWhenStuck) and reports it (onStuckChange). On Android the two cases are separate APIs: stickyHeader for headers of a lazy list, and the Scaffold's bars for content fixed to an edge. There is no stuck callback; the stuck state is derived from LazyListState, and a top app bar's scroll behavior already changes its color when content scrolls under it. The web's offset is the window insets, which Scaffold applies. iOS uses pinnedViews and safeAreaInset.
accessibility: System behavior: a sticky header is read once, in its place in the list order, not again while it is pinned.
Mark a sticky header as a heading so TalkBack's heading navigation jumps between groups.
Bars in a Scaffold are read before (topBar) or after (bottomBar) the content.
edgeCases: A sticky header with a transparent background lets rows show through it.
Forgetting the Scaffold's content padding puts the first and last rows behind the bars.
